packets.question: Which frontend architecture family best satisfies CMDR's first-party runtime, security, accessibility, deep-link state, performance and supply-chain requirements for INV-EVS-001?
constraints: No Case-link mutation while OPEN-013 is unresolved
CMDR-owned visual components; no third-party component kit
Minimize or eliminate third-party product-runtime JavaScript
Support currently used modern desktop browsers with graceful security fallback where a newer platform defense is unavailable

solution_families.name: First-party browser Web Platform application
solution_families.description: Client-side first-party ES modules, native Custom Elements where component boundaries help, standard DOM APIs, URL/History state and fetch/AbortController; no third-party UI runtime.
solution_families.rationale: Directly matches the deny-by-default runtime dependency constraint while retaining rich Event Search interactivity.

solution_families.name: Go server-rendered HTML with first-party progressive enhancement
solution_families.description: Server-rendered semantic HTML for the shell and states, enhanced by small first-party ES modules/custom elements for search execution, incremental updates and local interactions.
solution_families.rationale: Minimizes browser runtime and maximizes semantic HTML, but may increase server round-trips and split state ownership for a highly interactive search screen.

solution_families.name: Lit Web Components runtime
solution_families.description: Use Lit as a small third-party reactive Web Components runtime while keeping CMDR components and styling first-party.
solution_families.rationale: Provides declarative templates and targeted updates with a small runtime, but creates a third-party product-runtime dependency.

solution_families.name: Svelte compiled component architecture
solution_families.description: Use Svelte's compiler-oriented component model to generate browser code with fine-grained reactivity.
solution_families.rationale: Reduces manual reactive boilerplate and browser work, but introduces a third-party compiler/toolchain and generated framework coupling.

solution_families.name: React runtime architecture
solution_families.description: Use React and ReactDOM as the client rendering/state runtime, optionally with server rendering.
solution_families.rationale: Mature rich-interaction model and ecosystem, but adds a substantial third-party runtime/supply-chain surface that conflicts with CMDR's first-party-runtime preference.

claims.statement: The native browser primitives needed for a rich Event Search client are broadly established: ES modules, Custom Elements, History/URL state and AbortController do not require a third-party UI runtime.
Trusted Types can reduce DOM-XSS sink exposure but only reached MDN Baseline 2026, so CMDR cannot treat Trusted Types support as its sole XSS defense for older still-used browsers.
A first-party Web Platform implementation can have zero third-party UI runtime dependencies and therefore the smallest runtime supply-chain surface among the compared families.

A server-first progressive architecture can build on semantic native HTML controls and add first-party JavaScript only where interaction requires it, improving graceful degradation and accessibility foundations.
Lit is a Web Components helper runtime advertised at about 5 KB minified and compressed and performs targeted dynamic-part updates, but it remains a third-party runtime dependency.
Svelte uses a compiler-oriented UI model intended to do minimal work in the browser, reducing manual reactive boilerplate but adding a third-party compiler/toolchain and framework-generated coupling.

React supplies a rich client and server rendering runtime with concurrent and streaming features, but requires framework runtime packages and introduces framework-specific rendering/hydration semantics.
Event Search cancellation and deep-link state do not require a framework: AbortController can cancel fetch/stream consumption and History plus URLSearchParams can preserve URL-addressable state.
One-way incremental server updates can be delivered with broadly available Server-Sent Events if a later transport decision needs them; choosing SSE is not part of the frontend architecture decision.

limitations.statement: Broad availability does not prove CMDR's exact enterprise browser matrix; that matrix still needs an explicit supported-version policy and CI compatibility tests.
Eliminating a framework runtime shifts more rendering, state-management, virtualization and component lifecycle engineering onto CMDR and therefore requires strong first-party conventions and tests.
Trusted Types is a recent Baseline 2026 defense and may be unavailable on older still-used clients; safe DOM APIs and CSP remain mandatory independent defenses.
A server-first approach can increase request/round-trip dependence and split state between server HTML and enhanced client behavior for a highly interactive search workspace.
Lit is small but non-zero third-party product-runtime code, which conflicts with the strongest form of CMDR's internal-runtime preference and adds dependency review/update obligations.
Svelte reduces browser work through compilation but still creates reliance on an external compiler/toolchain and framework-specific generated semantics that must be revalidated on upgrades.
React's feature set and ecosystem do not remove its third-party runtime/supply-chain cost, and SSR/hydration adds additional framework-specific failure modes such as hydration mismatches.

Native URL/history/cancellation primitives solve transport and navigation mechanics but do not by themselves provide a disciplined application state model, rendering scheduler or large-table virtualization.
Custom controls still require explicit semantic roles, names, state exposure and keyboard behavior; native or custom-element architecture does not make accessibility automatic.
